thread.title: CEF ETB: The Undervalued Eaton Vance Option Fund - Eaton Vance Tax-Managed Buy-Write Income Fund (NYSE:ETB)

author: Nick Ackerman
title: CEF ETB: The Undervalued Eaton Vance Option Fund - Eaton Vance Tax-Managed Buy-Write Income Fund (NYSE:ETB)
text:
Eaton Vance Tax-Managed Buy-Write Income Fund ( ETB ) invests in a diversified portfolio of common stocks and writes call options on one or more U.S. indexes on a large portion of the value of its common stock portfolio. This is to help potentially generate option premium and enhance the yield the fund has to offer investors. The fund evaluates returns on an after tax basis and seeks to minimize and defer federal income taxes incurred by shareholders in connection with their investment in the fund.
ETB has a primary investment objective to provide current income and gains, with a secondary objective of capital appreciation.
I believe ETB is ripe for shareholders that are looking to add a quality option income fund at an enticing value. While the fund is currently at a slight premium of 1.06%, it is still "undervalued" when looking at the z-scores currently present in the fund.
Source - CEFconnect
A closed-end fund does not always have to be trading at a discount to be considered undervalued. Besides, buying a fund at a slight premium is sometimes the best a person can hope for when they are looking at quality funds. Of which, Eaton Vance has an excess of quality and can be viewed as one of the best in the CEF space.
I try to personally not make it a habit of buying a fund at a premium, my usual cut off point is anywhere from about 3-5%.
Distribution The distribution is also as attractive as the value ETB is showing. ETB has a distribution rate of 8.02%, and remember since this fund is at a slight premium, the distribution rate on the NAV will be slightly higher as well. The distribution rate on the NAV is currently showing a rate of 8.10%, not a huge difference but worth noting.
ETB is currently paying out on a monthly schedule at an amount of $0.1080. This has been the same distribution since January of 2013, prior to that date they had a quarterly schedule. The quarterly schedule was actually the same distribution just rolled up into a 3-month amount of $0.3240. They had even maintained that quarterly amount even further back to January of 2011. ETB held off cutting the distribution all the while through 08-09 mess, until they succumbed to an inevitable cut. This was typical of the vast majority of funds during that time and shouldn't be seen as a huge negative.
Having a long history of reliable and steady distributions is an income investors dream. Of course, it does not guarantee that the fund will not cut in the future as any fund is liable to do but seeing a long history can give some confidence.
Source - CEFconnect
Performance The fund has some attractive past performance numbers as well. While the fund currently trades at a share price of $16.16, with a NAV per share of $15.99. The fund is showing a market price slightly down from the beginning of the year, YTD the fund is at a return of -0.08%, while the NAV has a slight gain of 1.17%.
Looking further out at the 10-year performance mark, the fund is showing a NAV return of 8.24% and a market return of 9.38%.
Source - CEFconnect
You can compare this with the S&P 500 10-year returns of 9.75%; ETB is slightly lagging over that time period. But ETB is for an income investor, I didn't have to sell shares of say SPDR S&P 500 ETF ( SPY ) in order to use the "extra performance" the fund exhibited, it was paid out to an investor on a monthly basis.
Holdings The fund is currently weighted heavier towards tech and financials. These could be seen to benefit if the economy continues to expand.
Source - CEFconnect
The financial names should benefit as the Fed continues to raise interest rates, helping increase margins for financial entities like banks, insurance companies, and brokerage firms. The Fed raising rates is also associated with a strengthening economy.
Source - ETB Fund Website
Some notable holdings that I believe have strong catalysts for future growth would include the following:
Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) is of course a very well-known brand name, everyone probably thinks of their products as iPhones, Macs, or iPads. But after the iPhone segment Apple's next biggest business segment is Apple's services business. From Apple's second quarter release, services revenue jumped 31%, from $9.2 billion from $7 billion the following year. This is expected to big a huge driver of growth for Apple going forward, no longer relying as heavily on just iPhone sales.
Microsoft Corp. ( MSFT ) is definitely not standing still either, they are looking for ways to drive growth as well. Microsoft is of course well known for their computer software, such as Windows OS, Microsoft Office, and Internet Explorer browser. They have been making pushes into the cloud business through their cloud service, Azure. Azure is second only to Amazon's cloud service, Amazon Web Service. They announced in their 3rd quarter earnings that their server products and cloud services revenue increased 20%, due to 93% growth in Azure revenue. Azure has posted over 90% growth for the past 10 quarters.
And speaking of Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN ), ETB holds AMZN as well. While Microsoft's Azure has been taking market share away from Amazon's AWS, they have still been able to remain on top. AWS revenue still grew 49% from 2017 Q1. During their Q1 earnings they had announced their intentions of raising their Prime Membership fee as well by 20%, to $119 annually. They had just topped 100 million Prime members in April as well.
Basically, ETB is holding quality companies with the potentially for huge growth going forward.
What Do They Mean By "Tax-Advantaged" And Deferring Income Taxes? They are able to defer income taxes on the distributions as the fund pays out large amounts of ROC. The ROC that is utilized in the fund's distribution is a consequence of their option strategy that they deploy. As option premium is not classified as income or capital gains when it is distributed by the fund to shareholders; the option premium the fund collects is then classified as ROC. When ROC is used properly by funds that utilize an option strategy you will see the NAV remain steady or rise as the fund earns the premiums to pay out to shareholders.
This ROC that is used for their distribution will then reduce a shareholders cost basis in the fund, thus, deferring taxes until a shareholder sells the shares and pays capital gains taxes on the shares. Some shareholders can utilize these types of funds in taxable accounts to gain a sort of tax benefit, while the whole distribution isn't going to be deferred, a large portion will be from option funds. For example when looking at ETB's distribution tax character in their latest Annual Report you can see the prior year's breakdown.
Source - Annual Report
For 2017 approximately 88% of the distribution was classified as ROC, on a per share basis this would equate to $1.146. This amount would then reduce a shareholders cost basis by the $1.146. This goes on until the cost basis reaches all the way to $0 , then any subsequent distribution that is classified as ROC will be taxed at a holder's capital gains rate. This would most likely be long-term capital gains, as in most cases it would take longer than a one year period to reduce the basis all the way to $0.
I would like to note here though that I am not a tax professional. I am not trying to give any advice or guidance on specific tax situations and one should consult with a tax expert for their own situation.
Conclusion I would be a buyer of ETB here, with an attractive monthly distribution of 8% and being undervalued on a z-score basis. ETB is very similar to ETV, which I had covered favorably in the past. However, I wouldn't be selling ETV to purchase ETB because I like both funds. This would be a purchased as an additional position.
I believe that ETB has shown strong success in the past and will continue to do so in the future, as I believe they are in the right sectors for strong growth going forward. The distribution even has some potential for tax benefits for certain investors.
Eaton Vance is a top notch CEF provider with a strong history of success to boot.
